sections.title: General / cross-cutting
sections.note: How the document set itself behaves, and who builds it.

questions.why: I started BRIDGE-STD-001/2/3. Worth settling before there are ten of them.

opts.d: Standards sit beside ARCH-00N as their own series.
Number them as Reference chapters instead, 1–15 per the reading order.
One document, everything folded in as appendices.

questions.q: How should the Reference be assembled?

opts.d: Single markdown document, everything in it.
What we are already doing; easier to revise a chapter without touching the rest.

opts.t: Chapters, plus a generated single file
opts.d: Both — author per chapter, build a combined document for reading or printing.

questions.q: Hungarian language policy for the Reference?
questions.why: ARCH-002 exists in HU; the new standards are English.

opts.d: Every chapter in both. Doubles maintenance.
One glossary mapping every BRIDGE term, so you can talk to trades in Hungarian.
No HU material at all.
What the corpus already uses.
Major/minor/patch; clearer about whether a change breaks anything.
Revision is the date. Simple, no judgement needed.

questions.why: ARCH-002 §2.3 fixes ten colours. Amber/yellow and the two teals are close together.

opts.d: No change.
New palette, maximally separable. Breaks consistency with existing drawings.

opts.t: Keep, add hatch patterns as redundancy
opts.d: Colour stays; every layer also gets a line style, so a mono print still reads.

questions.q: Label hardware for conduits and boxes?
questions.why: The SELV standard requires durable machine-printed labels; it does not say which.

opts.d: Survives plaster dust and years. The trade standard.
Cheap, legible, less durable at cut ends.
Permanent, slow, expensive; right for the cabinet only.

questions.why: STD-001 §3.3 requires photographing every run before closing. Those photos need a home with the room reference.

opts.d: Simple, works today, no build effort.
Room and device records already exist there; as-builts attach to them.
Formal, good for handover, poor for ongoing edits.

questions.why: Changes the register of the Reference — a document for an electrician reads differently from one for you.

opts.d: Including MAINS.

opts.t: Electrician for MAINS, you for SELV + data
opts.d: The split the SELV standard implicitly assumes.
You specify, they build. Highest documentation burden.

sections.title: STD-001 — Physical standardisation
sections.note: Dimensions, zones, conduit and sequence. Confirm or correct the numbers I chose.

questions.q: RB-S at 90 mm internal depth cannot take full-depth DIN gear. Accept, or change?

opts.d: RB-S stays shallow: terminals, compact PSU, sub-controller, 4 compact relays.

opts.t: Raise all classes to 110 mm minimum
opts.d: One depth rule, every class takes any gear. Slightly deeper chase everywhere.
RB-M is the smallest box in the house. Simplest schedule, more volume in small rooms.
Consumer-unit standard: 45 mm device + 80 mm wiring.
Easier wiring and bend radius; fewer rows per box.
More rows; tight for anything but terminals.

questions.q: Horizontal module — 18 mm or true DIN 17.5 mm?
questions.why: DIN modules are nominally 17.5 mm; consumer units are commonly laid out on 18 mm.

opts.d: Matches how the BRIDGE-DN cabinet is already drawn.
True DIN; more modules per box, and matches device datasheets exactly.

questions.q: Zone order — sensors low, mains high?
questions.why: Air flows bottom to top, so heat sources belong high. But mains entry from below is the conventional habit.

opts.d: As drafted. Thermally and electromagnetically correct.
Familiar to any electrician; PSU heat then rises through every other zone.

questions.q: Where does the Z4 RF column go?

opts.d: Full height, behind an RF window, isolated from Z1.
Highest position for antennas; adjacent to the mains zone, which is worse for EMI.
Radios leave the RoomBox entirely — best RF, one more enclosure per room.

questions.why: IR is the one element in the box with a hard line-of-sight requirement, and it sets where the RF window goes.

opts.d: No extra endpoint; line of sight limited to whatever the box faces.

opts.t: Separate ceiling IR emitter on an ARM
opts.d: Proper coverage; one more endpoint and conduit.
Window emitter as standard, ceiling emitter where a TV or split unit needs it.
As drafted.
More growth room; pushes classes up a size.
Fill as needed, accept rework later.
Takes coax, fibre, audio.
Takes anything including a future multi-core bundle. Small cost now, large option later.
Two independent futures rather than one big one.

questions.q: A dedicated fibre conduit to each RoomBox now?

opts.d: Sixth conduit in the bundle.
Fibre pulls into the spare when it is wanted.
Where 10 GbE might actually land.

questions.q: If KNX is not taken, what happens to the C5 position?

opts.d: Bundle order never shifts; a later KNX run has a defined slot.
Cheapest time to do it is now.
Four conduits, and KNX is off the table for good.

questions.q: Corridor side convention for MAINS vs the CHANNEL bundle?

opts.t: Fixed — MAINS always the same hand
opts.d: Pick once, document it, never think again.
Decide per corridor on site.
Rule follows the plumbing instead of a convention.
As ARCH-002. Out of sight, above furniture, above most hazards.
Far easier to work in. Visible, and within reach of children.
Effectively invisible; needs a step for every service visit.
Robust, shields EMI, needs an RF window cut.
RF-transparent, disappears into the wall, vents easily.
Most discreet, slowest to open.
Reads as wall. Needs good documentation to ever find again.
Honest, findable, reads as technical.
Hidden in a wardrobe or cabinet. Best looking, worst access.
Standard, sealed, defined positions.
Fast, flexible, no sealing.
Fixed count and size, decided at manufacture.
As drafted — enough to re-terminate once.
Enough to re-terminate repeatedly or relocate a rail.
Tidiest, no second chances.
No noise, no moving part to fail in a wall.
The one box that may carry a real heat load.
Runs rarely; still a bearing in a wall cavity.
As drafted; loses 20% of thermal budget.
Better thermals, more ingress risk.
Sealed to water, vents vapour — stops condensation without losing rating.
One class, three documented variants.
Flatter; five classes become seven.
Variant recorded in the room schedule, not the class name.

questions.q: Where does PANEL LINK physically live, given BRIDGE-DN V2 is full?
questions.why: This is C3. Three real answers.

opts.d: A technical Edge RoomBox hosts the metering gallery.
Dedicated enclosure, DIN rail, conventional.

opts.t: Measuring gallery above the existing unit
opts.d: ARCH-002 variant B, built as drawn.

questions.why: U1. The Planner shares this namespace, so it has to be decided jointly.

opts.d: Flat and short: R03-A2.
Layer visible in the name: R03-LV-2. Self-documenting, longer.
Position-coded: R03-N2. Finds things physically.
R03-E07. Shortest, says nothing.
R03-L2 lamp, R03-S4 socket. Readable at a glance.
Encodes wall and height. Most informative, least stable if things move.
Dependency-ordered; no step needs a later one.
Third-party conduit goes in with first fix, so nothing is forgotten.
Radios in before sensor endpoints.

questions.q: How many universal endpoint positions per room?
questions.why: UEPs are the cheapest future-proofing in the design and the easiest to under-provide.

opts.d: Modest.
More generous; the cost is a flush box and a conduit.
Leanest; relies on getting the schedule right first time.
As drafted.
Easier pulls, more boxes to hide and document.
By bend count and cable stiffness.
As drafted.
Safer against screws and drills; needs the floor buildup to allow it.
Calculated per room.
Cat6A ≈ 65–75 mm. The cable standard's own figure.
Headroom for stiffer future cable. Larger sweeps to accommodate.

questions.q: Where does the conduit and cable schedule live?

opts.d: Works today.
Rooms, devices and paths already modelled there.
One document; goes stale fastest.

sections.title: STD-002 — Light and scene
sections.note: Photometry, the 24 V rail, scenes, and which integrated lighting is actually in scope.

opts.d: Perceptually linear slider. Needs a per-fixture correction against DALI gear.
Close enough, familiar from displays.
One curve across all gear; non-DALI channels emulate it.

questions.q: Minimum level for egress and night light?

opts.d: As drafted. Drives driver selection.
Genuinely dark-adapted night light. Narrows driver choice sharply.
Widest product choice; will feel bright at 3 a.m.
Clear of IEEE 1789 entirely.
Camera-safe by default; more EMI care on long runs.
Only if nothing is ever filmed. Still inside low-risk at modest depth.

questions.q: PWM or CCR as the default dimming method?

opts.t: PWM default, CCR in filmed rooms
opts.d: Cost-effective, colour-stable, with CCR where it matters.
Flicker-free by construction; dearer, slight warm shift at low level.
Cheapest and simplest; accept banding on camera.

questions.q: Which rooms count as filmed spaces?

opts.t: None — I do not film indoors

questions.q: Colour fidelity target in primary living space?

opts.d: As drafted; task areas stricter at 95/90.
Uniformly excellent. Costs more, narrows choice, no bad fixtures.
Widest product range, visibly duller reds.
Pink forgiven, green rejected. Tighter than the standard.
Simpler to state, lets some green through.
Accept anything compliant; some product will look green.
Mid-mix Duv ≈ −0.003, inside tolerance, covers the useful range.
Near-perfect locus tracking, very little range.
Full range, mid-mix ≈ −0.009 and visibly pink.

questions.q: Which rooms are tunable white at all?
questions.why: Fixed-CCT fixtures are cheaper and simpler. Tunable earns its place where people spend hours.

questions.q: Where is a three-channel locus-tracking fixture justified?

opts.d: As drafted; a step is invisible.
Much wider supply, a faint step may show on a white ceiling.
Cove and under-cabinet held to the tightest bin available.
White always from white LEDs; colour is an accent layer.
Tunable white only. Calmer, cheaper, less to go wrong.
Maximum flexibility, risk of a house that looks like a games room.

questions.q: Which rooms get a colour-capable accent layer?
Manual hold-off duration after someone overrides a scene by hand?
questions.why: The single biggest source of irritation in an automated house.

opts.d: As drafted.
Automation returns sooner; may feel pushy.
Automation never reasserts on its own. Maximum respect, risk of a room stuck in a stale state.
Effectively the rest of the evening.

questions.q: Should the hold-off end early when the room empties?

opts.d: As drafted. A fresh arrival gets automation back.
Predictable; the override survives you leaving the room.
Middle ground.
≈30 Wh usable; covers a normal outage comfortably.
Covers a long outage; larger pack per room or a bigger central one.
Enough to find a torch and get down the stairs.

questions.q: Where does the Bus B battery live?

opts.d: Fully distributed, survives anything local; many packs to maintain.

opts.t: One central pack feeding an assured 24 V bus
opts.d: One battery to maintain and test; depends on the assured bus surviving.

opts.t: Both — central pack, small local buffer
opts.d: Most robust, most hardware.

questions.q: Egress fallback level when the hardwired relay fires?

opts.d: Clearly visible, dark-adapted eyes cope, long battery life.
Confident light for an unfamiliar visitor; halves autonomy.
Just enough to navigate; longest runtime.
Capacity trend visible; alerts before failure.
Less battery wear, slower to spot degradation.
No automatic discharge; relies on you remembering.
Mains and architectural fixtures on DALI; all tape direct from Z2.
One addressable system, failure reporting throughout, higher cost per point.
Direct relay, PWM and 0–10 V only. Simplest, no addressability.
The house warms and dims through the day without being asked.
On where it helps — bedroom, living — off in utility spaces.
Scenes only, no background drift.
Navigable without waking anyone.
Easier to see; may disturb a light sleeper.
Egress on the landing only.

questions.q: Which linear / architectural lighting types are in the first build?
questions.why: Picking these narrows the fixture schedule and the conduit count immediately. Continued in C23B.

questions.q: Which feature and outdoor lighting types are in the first build?

opts.d: Indirect, even, flattering. Needs ceiling detail designed in.
Conventional, cheap, hard shadows and a drilled ceiling.
No architectural light; most flexible, least controllable.
Warmer, more candle-like.
Very warm; can look dingy on cool-toned walls.
Alerting without feeling clinical.
Strongest circadian signal, harshest look.
Gentler; weaker morning cue.
500 lx worktop and desk, 300 lx vertical at the vanity.
Serious cooking light.
Softer house, more reliance on task lamps.
Off, Egress, Night, Morning, Day, Evening, Task, Film, Guest, Clean.
Off, Night, Day, Evening, Task. Less to configure and maintain.
Each room gets what suits it. Most work, best fit.

questions.q: Certified emergency luminaires on the stairs, in addition to BRIDGE egress?
questions.why: BRIDGE egress is supplementary by design. Stairs are where the real risk is.

opts.d: EN 1838 / EN 60598-2-22 on their own supply, alongside BRIDGE.
Accept the supplementary level.
Settle what OTSZ actually requires here before deciding.

opts.t: Bistable relay per lamp in Z1
opts.d: As ARCH-002 and the ζ/η families. Manual-first guaranteed in hardware.
What BRIDGE-DN already uses; fast to build, firmware-dependent fail-safe.
No relays; everything addressable and dimmable. Loses the hardware bistable.

sections.title: STD-003 — Presence and identity
sections.note: Portals, fusion, Trinity, and audio that follows. The weights and thresholds are drafts — correct them.

opts.d: Direction, count and pet discrimination. Two ToF per door.
Direction everywhere, counting only where it matters. Cheaper, loses the count constraint.
Door contacts only. The graph becomes weak and the veto unreliable.

questions.q: Which openings get P-3 (portal + mmWave + thermal)?

opts.d: Cheap, I²C, one range per sensor. Enough for direction and height.
Profile and shape; distinguishes abreast crossings. Dearer, more processing.

opts.t: Mixed — L5CX at entry, L1X elsewhere
opts.d: Spend the resolution where crossings are complex.

questions.q: ToF pair spacing above the opening?

opts.d: As drafted; good direction resolution at walking pace.
Cleaner separation, needs a deeper lintel reveal.
Direction inferred from contact timing. Cheapest, least reliable.

questions.why: It drives the ToF choice and a good deal of the fusion tuning.

opts.t: Possibly in future — design for it

questions.q: The graph veto — a zone with zero counted occupants overrides a lone sensor?

opts.d: Structural cure for mmWave ghosting.
Simpler, ghosting returns.
Strongest constraint; a missed crossing then blinds a room until reconciliation.

questions.q: Sensor–graph disagreement window before the sensor is trusted?

opts.d: Faster correction, more churn.
Stabler, slower to recover from a missed crossing.

questions.q: Full reconciliation timeout (everything resets to zero)?

opts.d: Very conservative.
Fast recovery, risk of zeroing a still occupant.

questions.q: A portal held open — when do its two zones merge?

opts.d: Zones stay distinct; counts drift when doors live open.
Quicker to reflect reality, more merging churn.
2 min hall to 30 min bedroom.
More responsive, more wrong turn-offs.
Never caught out, more wasted light and heat.
Cheapest, fully open, raw data available, most tuning work.
PoE, dual radar, native ESPHome, local. Fits the architecture exactly.
Best zoning and polish; configuration needs the vendor app and cloud.
PIR + mmWave, fully tunable in HA, retail-assembled.

questions.why: It converts the hardest presence case in the house into the easiest.

opts.d: Where a camera is unacceptable but fall detection matters.
As drafted — highest fusion weight, narrowest deployment.

questions.why: CO₂ is the best long-window occupancy evidence in the house.

opts.d: On-device events, no audio ever transmitted.
Volume threshold, no classification. Least capable, least sensitive.
Rules out voice control and acoustic corroboration.

opts.t: Pursue now as an experimental signal
opts.d: Low fusion weight until validated in situ.
Reserve the idea; build the proven layers first.

questions.why: Three anchors per room, in the L-pattern corners already specified.

opts.d: Tune against real behaviour after commissioning.
Say which in the note.
Three or four sensors only, add weight classes later.
Harder to declare occupied; fewer false positives, more false vacancies.
Quicker to respond, more ghosting.
As proposed.
Name them in the note — watch, bag, badge?
Phone and keychain. Weaker claim, less to carry.
Cheap, years of battery, works with ESP32 proxies you already have.
Precise position as well as presence; dearer, shorter battery life.
No passive presence at all; defeats the point of carrying them.
BLE on all three, UWB added to the keychain.

questions.q: T3 threshold of 18 points, with at least one active factor?
questions.why: Three of three tags gives 14 — deliberately short of 18, so tags alone can never unlock a door.

opts.d: Two active factors for T3. More secure, more friction.
Convenient, and carried tags start to approach door-opening authority.
Meaningfully harder to guess, still quick to enter.
Short PIN, rising delay after failures.
As drafted.
Less to lose, weaker pattern learning.
Drop the behavioural factor entirely.

questions.why: STD-003 §4.4 makes your own server the root of recovery, which makes it a dependency.

opts.d: Name it in the note.
New dependency, deliberately provisioned and monitored.
Recovery requires physical access to COMP. Simplest and safest; you must be at home.

opts.t: On, excluding bath and quiet-hours bedroom
opts.d: As drafted.
Per-room audio only, no handoff.
Needs identity at T1+ to apply.
Ceiling for the follow-me layer, wall or floor for the living-room front stage.
Invisible throughout, no real stereo image anywhere.
Better imaging, visible speakers in every room.
